terms.definition: The agent declines to answer or act when evidence, confidence, or policy thresholds are not met — rather than guessing.
terms.scopeNote: Can improve calibration and reduce hallucination symptoms at the cost of task completion rate.
terms.literatureNote: Reactive recovery patterns. SRE names (circuit breaker, rollback) linked in academicTerms where relevant.

terms.definition: Stopping repeated calls to a failing dependency or halting an agent loop after a threshold of errors, to prevent runaway cost and cascading wrong actions.
terms.scopeNote: Prevents recovery failure from unbounded retry.
terms.literatureNote: Reactive recovery patterns. SRE names (circuit breaker, rollback) linked in academicTerms where relevant.

terms.definition: An automated action that reverses or offsets partial effects of a failed step — for example cancelling a reservation, issuing a credit, or notifying downstream systems.
terms.literatureNote: Reactive recovery patterns. SRE names (circuit breaker, rollback) linked in academicTerms where relevant.

terms.definition: Switching to an alternate model, tool, data source, or simplified path when the primary path fails — with explicit signalling to operators or users where required.
terms.scopeNote: Should declare reduced capability so silent wrong action is not mistaken for full success.
terms.literatureNote: Reactive recovery patterns. SRE names (circuit breaker, rollback) linked in academicTerms where relevant.

terms.definition: Restoring system or workflow state to a prior safe checkpoint after a failed or harmful step.
terms.scopeNote: Charter recovery and corrective actions scope.
terms.literatureNote: Reactive recovery patterns. SRE names (circuit breaker, rollback) linked in academicTerms where relevant.

terms.definition: Limits on which tasks, tools, data, and sub-agents an agent may use when handing work to others — including scope, expiry, and evidence requirements on handoffs.
terms.scopeNote: Reduces coordination failure and authorization failure in multi-agent systems.
terms.literatureNote: Proactive patterns that improve realised reliability. Less standardised in benchmarks than failure or accuracy terms.

terms.definition: A non-bypassable step that enforces allow-lists, budgets, or human approval before sensitive actions execute.
terms.scopeNote: Bridges reliability by design and correction mechanisms when the gate triggers escalation.
terms.literatureNote: Proactive patterns that improve realised reliability. Less standardised in benchmarks than failure or accuracy terms.

terms.definition: Checking agent specifications, tool bindings, and workflow definitions for conflicts, missing dependencies, or policy violations before execution starts.
terms.scopeNote: Targets configuration errors while they are still static and fixable.
terms.literatureNote: Proactive patterns that improve realised reliability. Less standardised in benchmarks than failure or accuracy terms.

terms.definition: Binding evaluation and production behaviour to explicit versions of models, prompts, tools, and agent specifications so results are reproducible and comparable.
terms.literatureNote: Proactive patterns that improve realised reliability. Less standardised in benchmarks than failure or accuracy terms.
